title: 4.7. Understanding Citizenship: Introduction 🌐
content: 📌 ውድ የኢትዮፍሬሽ ተማሪዎች!እንኳን ወደ ክፍል 3 ትምህርታችን በሰላም መጣችሁ! 👋✨ ዛሬ ደግሞ የሲቪክስ እና ፖለቲካ ትምህርት እጅግ አስፈላጊ እና ማራኪ ወደሆነው Citizenship (ዜግነት) ርዕስ እንገባለን። ዜግነት ሲባል በህግ አወቃቀር፣ በይዘት፣ መብትና ግዴታን በማን ረገድ ምን ማለት እንደሆነ፣ እንዴትስ እንደሚገለፅ በስፋት እናያለን። ፈተና ላይ የሚያጋጥሙ ዋና ዋና ነጥቦችንም በጥንቃቄ አካተናል። እስከ መጨረሻው አብራችሁን ቆዩ! 👇👇 Brainstorming Question: • What does the term citizenship mean to you personally? • Is it just an ID card, or does it involve deep active participation? 👉ዜግነት (Citizenship) ሲባል በቀላሉ የህግ መታወቂያ መያዝ ብቻ ሳይሆን ከሀገር ጋር የሚኖር የጠበቀ የህግ፣ የፖለቲካ እና የማህበራዊ ግንኙነት ህያው መግለጫ ነው!

title: 4.7.1. Defining Citizenship (ዜግነትን መተርጎም) 📜
content: 📌 1. What is a Citizen? • Citizen: A person who is a legal member of a particular officially sovereign State, owing allegiance (ታማኝነት) to that State. • Entitled to specific prerogatives (መብቶች/ጥቅሞች) and encumbered with responsibilities (ኃላፊነቶች). 2. What is Citizenship? • The legal and formal means by which we determine whether a person is a legal member of a State. • Formal Level: The network of rules regulating the legal relationship regarding the acquisition and loss of nationality. • Substantive/Political Level: Beyond legal status, citizenship creates a condition of civic equality among those who possess it. Why is Citizenship Polysemic? • It is a polysemy term (has multiple meanings) depending on historical legacies, state political organization, ideologies, and socio-cultural context. • Common elements found across all definitions include: Rights, Duties, Belonging, Identity, and Participation. 👉Citizen ማለት የሀገር ህጋዊ አባል የሆነና ለሀገሩ ታማኝነትን የሚያሳይ ግለሰብ ሲሆን፤ Citizenship ደግሞ በግለሰቡ እና በሀገሪቱ መካከል ያለውን ህጋዊ፣ ፖለቲካዊ እና ማህበራዊ ግንኙነት (አባልነትን) የሚወስን ህግና ስርዓት ነው። 💡 Exam Focus: Remember that citizenship is a polysemic term (multiple meanings) but always retains 5 core elements: Rights, Duties, Belonging, Identity, and Participation!

title: i) Citizenship as a Status of Rights ⚖️
content: 📌 Citizenship as a Status of Rights: • Being a citizen makes a person a creditor of a series of rights. • Modern political discourse directly identifies citizenship with the enjoyment of rights. T.H. Marshall's (1998) Three Historical Generations of Rights: 1. Civil/Legal Rights: Rights necessary for individual liberty (exercised mainly in Courts). 2. Political Rights: The right to participate in political power as a voter or elected official (exercised in Voting booths, Legislatures, and Protests). 3. Social Rights: Rights guaranteeing public safety, health, education, and a decent life (exercised/disputed in Government buildings). Status vs. Active Practice: • Scholars like Oldfield, Mouffe, and Lister define citizenship as both a Legal Status (possessing rights) and an Active Practice (exercising agency). 👉በ T.H. Marshall አመለካከት መብቶች በ3 ደረጃ ያድጋሉ፡ Civil Rights (በፍርድ ቤት የሚረጋገጡ)፣ Political Rights (በምርጫ እና በፓርላማ የሚተገበሩ)፣ እና Social Rights (በትምህርትና ጤና ተቋማት የሚጠየቁ) ናቸው። 💡 Exam Hint: Match Marshall's 3 rights with their institutional forums: Civil → Courts | Political → Voting Booths | Social → Government Agencies!

title: Hohfeldian Incidents: Primary Rules (Liberty vs. Claim) 🔗
content: 📌 Hohfeld's Four Components of Rights (1978): Wesley Hohfeld categorized rights into 4 distinct incidents. The first two are Primary Rules (rules requiring people to perform or refrain from actions). a) Liberty Right (Privilege): • Freedom given to the right-holder to do something without obligations on others to assist. • The state cannot interfere unless it prevents harm to others. • Example: Right to movement (FDRE Constitution Art. 25–34). b) Claim Rights: • The inverse of liberty rights—imposes a corresponding duty/obligation on another party or the State. • Example: Right to wages from an employer, or state-funded health & education services (FDRE Constitution Art. 41(3&4)). 👉Liberty Right: ሌሎች ምንም እንዲያደርጉልህ ሳትጠይቅ በነፃነት የምትጠቀምበት መብት ነው (ለምሳሌ የመዘዋወር መብት)። Claim Right: ደግሞ ሌላኛው አካል ግዴታውን ሲወጣ የምታገኘው መብት ነው (ለምሳሌ ደመወዝ የማግኘት ወይም የህክምና አገልግሎት የማግኘት መብት)። 💡 Exam Focus: Liberty Right = Freedom from interference | Claim Right = Imposes a direct duty on others/State!

title: Hohfeldian Incidents: Secondary Rules (Power vs. Immunity) 🛡️
content: 📌 Secondary Rules: Specify how agents can introduce, change, or alter primary rules (liberties & claims). c) Power Rights: • Rights regarding the modification or cancellation of first-order rights and entitlements. • Citizen Example: FDRE Art. 40(1) (Right to sell/transfer private property) & Art. 33(3) (Right to renounce citizenship). • State Example: Government modifying legal rights through legislation. d) Immunity Rights: • The opposite of power rights—allows bearers to escape control because others lack the legal power to alter their normative situation. • Examples: Civil servants protected from arbitrary dismissal during government changes; protection against self-incrimination; prohibition of forced labor (FDRE Art. 18(3)). 👉Power Right: ህጋዊ መብትን የመቀየር፣ የመሸጥ ወይም የመተው አቅም ነው (ለምሳሌ ንብረትን መሸጥ)። Immunity Right: ሌሎች የእንተን ህጋዊ ሁኔታ እንዳይቀይሩት የሚከላከል ከለላ ነው (ለምሳሌ ከገደብ ውጪ በግዴታ እንዳትሰራ መከልከል)። 💡 Real-Life Scenario (Smart Phone Example): • Liberty: Using your phone freely. • Claim: Expecting others not to steal it. • Power: Selling or gifting your phone. • Immunity: Police cannot search your phone without a legal warrant!

title: ii) Membership and Identity (አባልነት እና ማንነት) 🤝
content: 📌 Membership in a Political Community: • Implies integration into a political community with a specific shared identity. • Traditional criteria: Shared territory, common culture, ethnic characteristics, or history. The Ideal vs. Mere Member ("Good Citizen"): • True/Good Citizens: Those who actively contribute to the well-being of their community and embody civic virtues. • Mere Members (Free-Riders): Those who enjoy benefits without embracing responsibilities or understanding civic values. • Awards and honors are bestowed by communities to celebrate 'good' citizenship as an exemplary conduct. 👉በዘመናዊ አረዳድ True Citizen (እውነተኛ ዜጋ) የሚባለው ህጉን አክብሮ ለማህበረሰቡ እድገት አስተዋፅኦ የሚያደርገው ነው፤ ጥቅምና መብት ብቻ የሚፈልገው ግን Mere Member (ተራ አባል) ይባላል። 💡 Exam Hint: Understand the key difference between a 'free-rider' (mere member) and a 'true citizen' who practices proper civic conduct!

title: iii) Participation: Minimalists vs. Maximalists 🗳️
content: 📌 The Central Role of Participation: Participation is the core engine of active citizenship. People realize their rights through decision-making engagement. Two Key Approaches to Civic Participation: 1. Minimalist Approach: • Characterized by basic, passive compliance with state rules. • Citizens focus private life and do only what is legally bare minimum (e.g., paying taxes without active public engagement). 2. Maximalist Approach: • Characterized by active, broad, and continuous engagement in public affairs and state politics. Passive vs. Active Citizenship (Agency): • Passive Beneficiaries: People who merely receive public services. • Active Agents: Citizens who participate in shaping the services and policies that affect their daily lives. 😅 Humor Break: Minimalist citizens are like movie viewers in a cinema—they just watch the film; Maximalists are the film directors making things happen! 👉Minimalist: ህግ አክብሮ በዝምታ የሚኖር ህዝብ ሲሆን፤ Maximalist: ደግሞ በሀገር ጉዳይ እና በፖሊሲ ውሳኔዎች ላይ በንቃት የሚሳተፍ ንቁ ዜጋ ነው! 💡 Exam Focus: Contrast Minimalist (passive obedience) vs. Maximalist (active agency and broad engagement)!

title: iv) Inclusion and Exclusion: Citizens vs. Foreigners 🌍
content: 📌 Citizens vs. Aliens (Foreigners): Not everyone living in a state is a citizen. Foreigners/aliens reside under authorized visas. Shared Rights & Obligations: • Both aliens and citizens share rights to life, movement, protection of the law, and duty to respect host country laws. Exclusive Rights and Duties reserved ONLY for Citizens: • Exclusive Rights: Right to own land, vote, be elected to office, and hold a national passport. • Exclusive Duties: Defending the Constitution and defending the national territory from foreign aggressors. 👉የውጭ ሀገር ዜጎች (Aliens) በሀገራችን የመኖር እና የህግ ከለላ የማግኘት መብት ቢኖራቸውም፤ የመመረጥ፣ የመምረጥ፣ መሬት የመያዝ እና ሀገር የመከላከል መብትና ግዴታ ለኢትዮጵያውያን ዜጎች ብቻ የተጠበቀ ነው! 💡 Exam Hint: Essay questions frequently ask to differentiate exclusive citizen rights from general human rights enjoyed by aliens!

title: Corporate Citizenship & Global Citizenship 🏢🌐
content: 📌 1. Corporate Citizenship (CC) & CSR: • Citizenship is not restricted to human individuals; corporations also act as 'citizens'. • Corporations have rights (profit maximization) and legal duties (paying tax, environmental compliance). • Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR): Going beyond formal duties to support social development (building schools, supporting healthcare, helping vulnerable groups). 2. Global / Cosmopolitan Citizenship: • Extends citizenship beyond the traditional boundaries of a single nation-state. • Refers to seeing every human being as a member of a global worldwide community with shared global obligations. 👉Corporate Citizenship: ድርጅቶች ግብር ከመክፈል ባለፈ ለማህበረሰብ እድገት አስተዋፅኦ የማድረግ ኃላፊነታቸውን ያመላክታል፤ Global Citizen: ደግሞ በዓለም አቀፍ ደረጃ እንደ አንድ የዓለም ዜጋ ማሰብን ያመለክታል። 💡 Exam Focus: Differentiate Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) from formal corporate duties (tax & law obedience)! --- 🎯 ❤️ ስለ ተከታተላችሁን እጅግ እናመሰግናለን! የትምህርት ክፍሉ በስኬት ተጠናቋል። በርቱልን ጀግኖቻችን! 🙏🙏🙏
